description: Source-bound editorial descriptions of visible content and treatment. Documentary meanings are separate from visual assignments.
limits: These are nonexclusive editorial descriptions of particular reproductions, reviewed by an assistant. They are not independent human validation, scientific scores or measurements of a viewer's feelings.
Only an explicit reviewed absent status supplies a negative observation. A missing review, mismatched source, unknown status or insufficient reproduction remains unknown.
Visible descriptions and museum-documented meanings are separate. Missing documentation never establishes that a work has no symbolism.
A shared attribute across several preferred or admired works is a descriptive pattern. It does not identify why the viewer chose them or a psychological cause.
A whole work can contain different treatments in different areas. A present feature does not establish that a viewer noticed or responded to it.
The reviewedAsset can offer more detail than the preview. These are descriptions of the artwork reproduction, not a reconstruction of the viewer's gaze or viewing conditions.

Current editorial interpretation may accompany an older response only when its original artwork source and preview identity are verified; it must be labelled as current interpretation, not a historical participant answer.
